one_line: A buyer-owned shoe fit profile that shopping agents can read and apply across stores.
what_it_does: Stores canonical foot-length ranges inferred from known-fitting shoes, then lets agents inspect, update, and compare products against that buyer profile.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP exposes structured buyer-side fit state that a general UI-driving agent would have to reconstruct and could misread across merchant catalogs.
leverage_evidence: Pitch centers on an agent-readable profile usable on any store without merchant integration.
About text describes canonical millimetre ranges, explicit conflict handling, and tools to read/write/check fit.
execution_rationale: The packet presents a coherent commerce workflow and multiple product/profile screens, though static frames do not prove the full live flow end to end.
execution_evidence: Facts report alive demo, public repo, five gallery images, and a 168-second video.
Frame sheet montage shows repeated coherent profile, catalog, and result UI states.
impact_rationale: It targets a concrete, costly shoe-sizing problem for shoppers and merchants, with a buyer-side data model that addresses cross-brand ambiguity.
impact_evidence: About text cites seven identical-label shoes spanning 7 mm and describes size/fit as a major source of returns.
Cross-store, cross-brand fit checking is the stated central use case.
creativity_rationale: The buyer-owned fit profile is a fresh complement to merchant-centered agent commerce protocols.
creativity_evidence: Concept explicitly models the buyer beyond payment and shipping address.
Labels resolve to canonical length ranges rather than naïve label-to-label conversion.
usability_note: Brand/size entry avoids requiring users to know millimetres and conflict messages appear useful.
red_flags: No transcript and static frames cannot independently verify live tool calls.
standouts: Strong buyer-side data model for agentic commerce.
advance_reason: High-impact, clearly differentiated WebMCP use with substantial claimed and visual evidence.

one_line: A headless layer that turns agent intent into guided clickable UI sequences.
what_it_does: Maps a typed request to a WebMCP tool once, then guides the human through deterministic clicks and drags rather than continued conversational guessing.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP provides the structured tool inventory and schemas needed for one-shot intent resolution; the product then converts that into reliable human interaction.
leverage_evidence: About text says Crystal reads site WebMCP tools and performs one AI match followed by a fixed sequence.
Forked Excalidraw has 14 tools mapped to real drawing functions.
execution_rationale: The concept and Excalidraw integration are coherent, with frame sheets showing editor/canvas states, but end-to-end completion is not directly demonstrated.
execution_evidence: Facts report alive demo and three frame sheets.
Frames show a consistent canvas/editor with changing colored component arrangements.
impact_rationale: It addresses a real usability problem in chat-driven spatial tasks by returning control to a guided interface, especially useful for complex canvas operations.
impact_evidence: About text identifies dropdown/clickable UI as preferable to text for spatial tasks.
Excalidraw provides a concrete real-world test surface.
creativity_rationale: The interaction model—AI chooses once, human executes a structured sequence—is a notably fresh alternative to agent command execution.
creativity_evidence: Explicitly separates model intent selection from human spatial action.
Includes refusal when no tool cleanly matches instead of hallucinating.
usability_note: Guided mouse steps can reduce ambiguity, though long sequences may become tedious.
red_flags: No submitted video despite referenced frame sheets.
advance_reason: Original, useful WebMCP-mediated interaction model with credible prototype evidence.

one_line: A shared durable workspace for researchers and agents to inspect evidence and run bounded experiments.
what_it_does: Unifies research graphs, evidence, conversations, artifacts, human decisions, and controlled experiment episodes behind a browser-native agent interface.
leverage_rationale: The agent can operate on structured research state and dispatch bounded workflows while the researcher watches the same durable workspace; this is materially beyond UI automation.
leverage_evidence: Pitch calls it a shared control plane with inspection and control.
About text describes one-call research operations, permissioned graph updates, experiment readiness, episode execution, and artifact retrieval.
execution_rationale: The packet describes an intentional multi-surface system and frames show a substantial dashboard, but the core experiment lifecycle is not visibly proven end to end.
execution_evidence: Alive demo and public repo are reported.
Frame sheets show research dashboard cards, tables, forms, and status views.
impact_rationale: Researchers have a real coordination and reproducibility problem, and the product directly addresses durable evidence, supervision, and bounded automation.
impact_evidence: About text identifies scattered repos, schedulers, artifacts, and chat history as the problem.
Hosted project is described as a reproducible continual-learning study.
creativity_rationale: Combining research graph, evidence provenance, human decisions, and bounded agent episodes into a shared control plane is ambitious and distinctive.
creativity_evidence: Research-level operations are exposed instead of generic CRUD.
Human permission remains part of the research graph workflow.
usability_note: Shared state and bounded operations are promising, but the surface appears information-dense.
red_flags: No video and no direct end-to-end episode evidence in the packet.
standouts: High WebMCP leverage through durable shared research state.
advance_reason: One of the strongest agent-native concepts: structured, bounded, supervised research operations.

one_line: An agent-native sprint planner where agents propose changes and humans approve them.
what_it_does: Lets agents read project context, propose requirements/sprints/tasks and edits, and stage a reviewable change set without direct writes.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP enables a conversational proposal-and-human-approval loop over live planning state; the deliberate no-write contract changes agent reliability and trust.
leverage_evidence: Pitch states no WebMCP tool ever writes to the plan.
Transcript shows proposed task movement appearing in a review panel for approval rather than direct mutation.
About text describes context, proposal, pending change-set, focus, and approval tools.
execution_rationale: The video transcript documents a coherent central workflow from sign-in through project inspection to staged task movement, with a clear product scope.
execution_evidence: 135-second video transcript includes live project lookup and review-panel proposal.
Facts report alive demo and video; frames show multiple planning-board states.
impact_rationale: Teams need planning assistance but also need confidence that an agent will not silently corrupt sequencing and estimates; approval gates address that directly.
impact_evidence: About text explains the risk of blind INSERT-style planning tools.
Product covers requirements, sprints, tasks, estimates, and review.
creativity_rationale: Treating agent calls as proposals that wait for human judgment is a strong interaction and governance innovation for project planning.
creativity_evidence: Explicit three-move loop of reading context, proposing, and human approval.
Tool behavior is designed around argument/review rather than CRUD.
usability_note: Review panel makes consequential changes legible; login adds friction.
red_flags: Transcript calls the product Sprintify/Sprintfy inconsistently.
standouts: Excellent evidence-backed approval workflow and safety boundary.
advance_reason: Strong demonstrated workflow plus a meaningful, well-articulated WebMCP design choice.

one_line: A browser-native execution firewall with human authorization and cryptographic audit ledgers.
what_it_does: Pauses risky WebMCP calls, applies deterministic policy, requires cryptographic human approval, and records SHA-256-linked audit history.
leverage_rationale: The browser-boundary interception and structured authorization/audit layer materially changes the safety properties of agent tool execution.
leverage_evidence: Pitch claims execution freeze at the browser boundary, dynamic policy, human-in-loop authorization, and SHA-256 audit chain.
Frame sheets visibly show dark authorization, console, and audit-style states.
execution_rationale: The packet is coherent and technically ambitious, but static technical screens do not prove that signing, blocking, and verification work correctly.
execution_evidence: Alive demo and public repo reported.
Frames show policy/configuration, authorization, logs, and cryptographic audit UI.
impact_rationale: Unauthorized financial or persistent-state mutations are a serious problem for agentic systems, and a browser-native control point could protect many tools.
impact_evidence: About text identifies prompt injection, runaway loops, and absence of proof as concrete threats.
Scope includes payouts, balances, quotas, and persistent state.
creativity_rationale: Perpendicular policy enforcement with cryptographic human intent proofs is an ambitious and memorable framing for WebMCP security.
creativity_evidence: Combines deterministic risk engine, execution freeze, and append-only hash chain.
Targets browser-native tool boundary rather than relying only on agent prompts.
usability_note: Strong safety controls may add approval friction; the packet does not show enough of the operator flow.
red_flags: No video; cryptographic claims are not independently verifiable from screenshots.
standouts: Addresses a consequential gap in agent execution safety.
advance_reason: High-impact infrastructure concept with visible prototype surfaces, though technical execution needs observation.

one_line: A natural-language decision engine that ranks food, grocery, and service options by user priorities.
what_it_does: Uses text, voice, or image requirements to find and explain three options, supports budget what-if scenarios, and routes users through confirmation and payment.
leverage_rationale: Structured agent decision support could reduce multi-constraint search friction, but the stated simulations and ordinary confirmation flow appear replicable by a general agent with some effort.
leverage_evidence: About text describes natural-language requirements, ranked compromises, explanations, and scenario simulation.
All simulations are explicitly based on example data only.
execution_rationale: The packet provides only a showcase screenshot and prose; no frame sheets or video evidence demonstrate the product workflow.
execution_evidence: Facts report 16 gallery images but no submitted frame sheets.
Devpost screenshot shows packaging only, not a running workflow.
impact_rationale: Choosing among food, grocery, and services is a recognizable user need, but the example-data-only limitation weakens demonstrated real-world value.
impact_evidence: Product targets multiple everyday purchasing/service decisions.
Description claims budget adjustment and requirement matching.
creativity_rationale: Multimodal preference-driven ranking and what-if simulation add a useful angle to a familiar recommendation category.
creativity_evidence: Supports chat, voice, image upload, and budget scenario changes.
Covers food, grocery, and service flows.
usability_note: The described guided flow is understandable, but evidence is too thin to assess polish.
red_flags: Only packaging screenshot in packet; simulations use example data only.
No frame sheets or video evidence submitted.
standouts: Multimodal requirement input and what-if budget exploration.
advance_reason: Potentially useful but lacks the visual/end-to-end evidence required for a strong Stage 1 advancement case.

one_line: Outcome monitoring that links agent shopping journeys to verified WooCommerce business results.
what_it_does: Records redacted agent journeys, missed demand, feedback, reversible cart activity, human checkout handoffs, orders, refunds, and evidence-backed analytics.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP is central: the product observes structured tool journeys and connects them to verified site outcomes while preserving shared workflow evidence and human checkout boundaries.
leverage_evidence: Transcript describes agent discovery, zero-result opportunity capture, recovery, cart, checkout handoff, verified order, and owner analytics.
About text details narrow WebMCP tools, redacted ledger, provenance, and no raw customer data.
execution_rationale: The transcript provides unusually complete end-to-end evidence from shopper request through order verification and merchant replay, supported by coherent frame sheets.
execution_evidence: 166-second transcript traces one workflow across search, recovery, cart, handoff, order, and analytics.
Facts report alive demo, public repo, 11 gallery images, and video.
impact_rationale: It gives merchants actionable visibility into agent conversion, unmet demand, evidence quality, and handoffs—an emerging operational gap with direct value.
impact_evidence: Transcript shows IPX5 unmet demand retained despite IPX4 recovery and verified order attribution.
About text distinguishes direct, assisted, and influenced revenue without double counting.
creativity_rationale: The combination of agent journey observability, evidence provenance, missed-demand signals, and verified commerce outcomes is an original product synthesis.
creativity_evidence: Captures zero-result demand even when agents provide no feedback.
Separates agent testimony from server-computed business facts.
usability_note: The owner-facing replay and evidence-linked analytics appear operationally useful.
red_flags: Some claims depend on the submitted demo transcript rather than independently observed execution.
standouts: Best end-to-end evidence and unusually disciplined provenance model.
advance_reason: Exceptional WebMCP leverage, impact, and end-to-end claimed execution with strong evidence.

one_line: A video library that lets an agent turn saved reels into searchable knowledge and tasks.
what_it_does: Processes saved videos, preserves shared page/agent state, and exposes project, search, memory, and task actions through WebMCP.
leverage_rationale: Shared UI/API state and bounded structured selectors improve agent reliability over asking an agent to repeatedly inspect video pages, though the core outcome remains achievable with other multimodal APIs.
leverage_evidence: About text says the agent shares apiRequest, navigate, and renderProject with the UI.
Nine tools map to existing actions and include schemas and content-safety annotations.
execution_rationale: The implementation description is concrete and the frames show a coherent video/task workspace, but the packet lacks a direct demonstrated conversion sequence.
execution_evidence: Public repo and alive demo reported.
Frame sheets show video/content lists, transcript-like areas, projects, and task controls.
impact_rationale: It addresses a common problem for people saving instructional or recipe videos and failing to retrieve actionable details later.
impact_evidence: About text gives concrete lost-link, install-step, tool-name, and ingredient-list use cases.
Product includes saved videos, memory, and task tracking.
creativity_rationale: Turning passive short-video saves into agent-queryable projects and actionable tasks is a fresh, useful synthesis.
creativity_evidence: Same backend and UI state are deliberately shared with the agent.
Personal MCP selector complements the page WebMCP surface.
usability_note: A unified saved-video-to-task workspace is intuitive, though processing complexity is unclear.
red_flags: No video transcript; static frames do not prove task creation from a video.
standouts: Concrete shared-state implementation rationale rather than a parallel agent API.
advance_reason: Good practical use case and credible WebMCP integration, with moderate evidence gaps.

one_line: A shared family care plan where agents can update medications, symptoms, appointments, and tasks.
what_it_does: Maintains a live caregiving plan and family feed that an older adult, relatives, and agents can read and update through structured tools.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP lets agents act on the live shared care plan rather than a screenshot or drifting copy, enabling coordinated updates across family views.
leverage_evidence: About text describes twelve structured tools for plan data, symptoms, medication notes, calls, tasks, and family updates.
Pitch emphasizes shared state visible to family and agents.
execution_rationale: The scenario is coherent and the frame sheets show care-plan/task states, but no video or direct end-to-end medical coordination proof is included.
execution_evidence: Alive demo, public repo, and three frame sheets reported.
Frames show care-plan forms/dialogs, checklist/task content, and status views.
impact_rationale: Family caregiving coordination is a serious, specific need; reducing scattered updates and helping relatives act on symptoms can have substantial value.
impact_evidence: About text gives a concrete dizziness/medication scenario with family tasks and pharmacist call.
Supports remote family members sharing one plan and asking about medication adherence.
creativity_rationale: The voice/text-to-live-care-plan model is a thoughtful application of agent state sharing to family caregiving.
creativity_evidence: Older adult, family members, and agent are modeled as distinct participants.
Family feed and live plan connect conversational input to coordinated action.
usability_note: Voice/text and role-based views fit the audience, but safety-sensitive flows need careful observation.
red_flags: Health/medication claims require strong safeguards; packet does not show them in detail.
advance_reason: Strong audience need and meaningful WebMCP collaboration, tempered by limited execution evidence and health-safety uncertainty.

one_line: A climate dashboard that generates queryable visual and audio views from natural-language questions.
what_it_does: Exposes climate datasets as WebMCP-backed semantic tools that compute attributed answers and mirror charts, highlights, warming stripes, and sonification into shared page state.
leverage_rationale: Structured data tools let agents obtain exact values, units, provenance, and synchronized visual state—capabilities a general screenshot-driving agent cannot reliably provide.
leverage_evidence: About text contrasts exact source-attributed answers with unreliable screenshot interpretation.
Examples include hottest year +1.28 C in 2024, chart highlighting, runtime tool families, and sonification.
execution_rationale: The concept is unusually coherent and detailed, but this packet includes no raw frames or video, so visual and end-to-end claims remain only partially evidenced.
execution_evidence: About text specifies 2,026 rows, four datasets, query-to-chart behavior, and multiple output modes.
Facts report alive demo and public repo, but no submitted frame sheets.
impact_rationale: It makes climate evidence more interrogable and accessible, including for people who cannot rely on conventional chart visuals.
impact_evidence: About text identifies exact-value/provenance and screen-reader accessibility gaps.
Supports charts, tables, warming stripes, and audio sonification from the same data.
creativity_rationale: Query-driven climate visualization plus synchronized sonification and runtime tool families is a memorable, ambitious interaction model.
creativity_evidence: The dashboard starts with data and no preset answers, then builds views from questions.
Sonifies 146 years with a peak cue and keeps outputs queryable.
usability_note: Natural-language interrogation and multimodal output could serve both accessibility and exploration, pending live verification.
red_flags: No frame sheets or video submitted; visual claims cannot be checked directly from packet imagery.
advance_reason: Exceptional creativity and WebMCP fit; execution score is capped by missing visual/video evidence.
